opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new medicines — up 8%, driven by continued investments in the early and late-stage pipeline.

opex.name: Marketing, selling & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, advertising and running the company — up 26%, mainly promotional efforts supporting ongoing and future launches.

opex.name: Acquired IPR&D
opex.note: Research bought in from other companies, expensed on the spot — mainly Scorpion Therapeutics' STX-478 program this quarter.

opex.name: Asset impairment & restructuring
opex.note: Charges related to intangible asset impairments.

follow100Note: Mounjaro and Zepbound together supplied $48.34 of every $100 Lilly took in — two versions of the same drug, tirzepatide. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Reported (GAAP) figures throughout; Lilly's non-GAAP net income was $3,004M (EPS $3.34), and both reported and non-GAAP EPS include the $1.72 of acquired IPR&D charges.
oneTimers: Acquired IPR&D charges of $1,572M — primarily the acquisition of Scorpion Therapeutics' PI3Kα inhibitor program STX-478 — expensed in full this quarter. They account for $1.72 of EPS and, being largely non-deductible, pushed the effective tax rate up to 20.2%.

Jardiance revenue included a one-time benefit of $370M from an amendment to the Boehringer Ingelheim collaboration that adjusted who sells Jardiance in certain markets — that benefit sits inside 'All other medicines' revenue.
Asset impairment, restructuring and other special charges of $35M, related to intangible asset impairments.
otherDetail: Net other expense of $239M — net interest expense of $195M, plus $44M of net other expense, including losses on investments in equity securities.

segments.name: Mounjaro
segments.note: The diabetes shot (tirzepatide) — sales more than doubled, with U.S. revenue up 75% to $2.7B and revenue outside the U.S. up to $1.2B as it entered new markets, partly offset by lower realized prices.

segments.name: Zepbound
segments.note: The weight-loss shot sold in the U.S. — sales more than quadrupled on increased demand, partly offset by lower realized prices.

segments.name: All other medicines
segments.note: Everything else Lilly sells, including Verzenio at $1.2B and Jardiance at $1.0B — the Jardiance figure includes a one-time $370M collaboration benefit.

takeaways.text: Mounjaro ($3.8B, +113%) and Zepbound ($2.3B) together brought in $6.2B — 48% of all revenue. Volume rose 53% overall, partly offset by lower realized prices.
takeaways.title: Two drugs drove the growth

takeaways.text: Acquired IPR&D charges of $1.57B — mainly for Scorpion Therapeutics' STX-478 program — cost $1.72 of the quarter's $3.06 reported EPS. Because the charge is largely non-deductible, the effective tax rate rose to 20.2% from 11.6% a year ago.
takeaways.title: The bought-research charge

takeaways.text: Gross margin rose 1.6 points to 82.5% on improved production costs and a favorable product mix, partly offset by lower realized prices. Lilly reaffirmed full-year 2025 revenue guidance of $58.0–61.0B.
takeaways.title: Margins widened, guidance held

verdict: Lilly's revenue jumped 45% to $12.7B as Mounjaro and Zepbound sales surged — but a $1.6B charge for research bought from Scorpion Therapeutics held reported profit growth to 23%, at $2.8B.
